title: Tofu Katsu Sando with Tangy Katsu Sauce and Sesame Cabbage
summary: Crisp panko-coated tofu slabs layered with tangy sesame cabbage and a sweet-savoury sauce between soft white bread, a vegetarian take on the classic sando.
equipment: wire rack set in a tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Whisk 60 g ketchup, 4 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tsp soy sauce, 1 tsp garlic powder and ½ tsp sugar together.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Whisk the 2 eggs with 2 tbsp flour in one dish and crush 75 g panko into a second dish, then cut the 400 g tofu into 8 slabs, pat dry, season with ½ tsp salt, dip in egg and press into the panko.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high and fry the tofu until deep golden, 2-3 min per side, then drain briefly on paper and move to a rack.

steps.title: Cabbage
steps.text: Toss the shredded cabbage with 2½ tsp rice vinegar, 1½ tsp sesame oil and the remaining sugar.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Layer bread, cabbage, 2 tofu slabs and sauce, then top with a second slice of bread.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Press lightly, trim the crusts, halve and serve.

tips: Pat the tofu dry before coating so the egg and panko stick properly.
Fry in a single layer so each slab crisps evenly on both sides.
Trim the crusts after assembling so the layers stay neat when cut.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best assembled and eaten straight away while the tofu is still crisp. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
